_comment: REGRESSION GUARD for the 'none' exemption at schema_version 3. The fail-closed empty-tally rule reaches every algorithm OTHER THAN 'none' (RFC-MACP-0012 4.1), and the decline guard and face-value exception of RFC-MACP-0007 6.2 likewise do not reach it. Before this fixture the only 'none' fixture in the corpus declared schema_version 2, so a runtime that swallowed 'none' into the fail-closed arm passed every fixture in the repository while breaking decision_critical_objection_finalize_decline.json's premise. This fixture pins the NEGATIVE direction, which was the bare cell: the only fixture pinning 'none' + empty tally + negative was at schema_version 2. Its sibling decision_none_v3_empty_tally_positive.json pins the positive direction.
description: Decision Mode: 'none' is unaffected by the schema_version 3 empty-tally rule -- a NEGATIVE commitment seals on zero ballots, with no decisive REJECT, via RFC-MACP-0007 6.2's face-value exception.

policy.description: No voting constraint, initiator-only commitment, schema_version 3. Pins that 'none' is exempt from the fail-closed empty-tally rule.

messages._comment: THE OTHER HALF OF THE EXEMPTION. RFC-MACP-0012 4.1 says the empty-tally rule and the decline guard both do NOT reach voting.algorithm 'none', and RFC-MACP-0007 6.2's face-value exception takes outcome_positive at face value with no decline guard -- in BOTH directions. So a negative commitment also seals here on zero ballots, with no decisive REJECT anywhere in history. Before this message the corpus pinned 'none' + empty tally + NEGATIVE only at schema_version 2 (decision_critical_objection_finalize_decline.json), so a runtime that swallowed the negative direction into the fail-closed arm under schema_version 3 passed every fixture in the repository.
